rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing ([[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)").

Columbia was Apollo 11's command module ([[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"). The command and service module was built by North American Aviation ([[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)").

The company that built the spacecraft Collins stayed in was therefore North American Aviation. It was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module ([[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)").

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters of Oxygen tank No. 2 were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours before launch. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report named the switch failure as the cause. It called that failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not give a fact line that says the board named the thermostatic switches as the start of the fire in those words. The switch link rests on the report line above.

rows.question: Which Apollo 11 crew member earned a doctorate on the kind of rendezvous Apollo relied on, and in which year?

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The measles exposure came from Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot. The swap that followed brought in Jack Swigert in place of Ken Mattingly. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" and [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" and [[ken-mattingly]] "[stated] Assigned to Apollo 16 as command module pilot (was Apollo 13 command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)".

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but he died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The notes do not give the cause or date of his death, or which House seat he was elected to.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was the Apollo 13 CO2 scrubber adapter, an improvised part that fitted the command module's square lithium hydroxide canisters into the lunar module's round-socket system. Engineers devised it from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape, and the crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"; [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The square-versus-round mismatch is stated as: [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not give the exact sequence of steps the crew used to assemble the adapter, or the specific dimensions and parts.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
The earlier citations dropped the `[stated]` tag that starts each fact line. Here they are copied in full, without the leading `- `:

1. **1970-04-10: the crew swap.** A KSC management meeting replaced Ken Mattingly with Jack Swigert as command module pilot, announced at a press conference that day. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)" The swap followed blood tests showing Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-11: launch.** [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-13: explosion and abort.** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)" The same day the mission goal changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-17: splashdown.** The crew, having used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **June 1970 (day not recorded): review board report.** The Cortright board published its report, which traced the explosion to the oxygen tank's switches. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
